the fleet holds one workspace copy per VM (50 x 16 MiB of image)

notes: 50-VM --workspace boot (POST -> running): 1365ms
fleet 50 with workspace: RSS baseline 4 MiB peak 5880 MiB; CPU [2.25, 2.25, 1.75]% of one core

the 800 MiB of copies are host memory, not guest RSS: this host's harness work directory is under /tmp (tmpfs), so their pages are charged to Shmem — which went 7187 -> 8000 MiB (12 MiB off the copies' 800 MiB) while the fleet ran. Host-wide Cached (45792 -> 46284 MiB) moved for the whole host's reasons and is not attributed to the fleet. noded's RSS is what the 8 GiB criterion measures and does not carry the copies, so a fleet's true host cost is that RSS plus them — recorded here so it is not understated

steady-state CPU with the volume attached is 2.250% of one core versus 2.2499645478585073% without it in this run: the guest's ext4 journal adds no measurable steady-state cost here (the case without a workspace carries the 0.03%-baseline finding)

findings.title: steady-state CPU does not reproduce the recorded 0.03% baseline
findings.detail: measured peak 2.250% of one core for 50 guests with the fleet's own beats configuration versus the 0.03% recorded in PORT_STATUS slice 16. The configured bar (5.0%) still passes, with a thin margin. At n=2 the same configuration measures 0.000%. The recorded figure was sampled with the guests 'parked in HLT', which measures no heartbeat writes and no console polling; noded never boots a parked guest (its cmdline builder has no halt option), and every guest it does boot writes a heartbeat every 5 s and polls its console every second, plus the run watcher's 5 ms poll pass. Those wakeups are the measured cost. A like-for-like baseline is needed: either re-sample the recorded figure with the same guest configuration, or expose a parked-guest option through noded so both states can be measured.
